chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Meeting Luis Russell and Russell sending to Chicago for Oliver's men
summary: Playing the Nest Club he met Russell, who enlarged the band by sending for Pops Foster, Red Allen, Simeon and Barbarin and later got the band together at the Saratoga.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now, Russell must have been on piano.
Would you have remembered another alto player by the name of Paul Barnes?
Paul Barnes? Yes, that's the other alto player.
And the rest of it must have been Barbarin on drums...

Barbarin on drums. I don't know the guitar player's name. I didn't meet all of them. But they didn't stay around town too long. Most of them went back to Chicago, including Red Allen -- he went back, too.

Later, when I went to work at the Nest Club, then I met Luis Russell. That's when I met Luis Russell. But they were in a while... Then we decided to form a band, a bigger band than he had in the Nest Club. That's when he started enlarging his band, and he sent to Chicago for different ones...the members of King Oliver's band. He sent for Red Allen. He sent for Simeon, Omer Simeon. He sent for Paul Barbarin. The first one he sent for was Pops Foster. I don't know if Pops Foster was in that band or not. But Pops Foster was the first one he sent for. He came in '29. And he worked at the Nest, opposite (?).
Then we left the Nest, and we went I think to the Saratoga Club. That's where Russell got his band together at, with his Chicago boys. That's where... He recorded, he made a recording for...
Actually, you made one under Oliver's name, with the Russell band essentially.
Yeah. Essentially, it was really the Russell band... It was the Oliver band essentially, but...
